draft.title: Supply chains
card: A supply chain is every step a product takes from raw material to the buyer. Each step is done by a person or business, often in a different place.
Take a cotton T-shirt. Cotton is grown on a farm, spun into thread, woven or knitted into cloth, sewn into a shirt, shipped to a country, and sold in a shop.
Steps in a chain can be in different countries. Transport links the steps, so the chain connects the people and places along it.
A problem at one step, such as a flood closing a port, can delay or raise the cost of the steps after it.
draft.remember: A supply chain is the whole journey from raw material to buyer, and each step depends on the one before.

a.q: Which of these describes a supply chain for a cotton T-shirt?
opts: Growing, spinning, sewing, shipping and selling the shirt
The shop where the shirt is sold to the buyer
The farm where the cotton is grown for the shirt
The ship that carries the finished shirt overseas
a.why: A supply chain covers every step from raw material to buyer. The other options each name only one step, such as the farm or the shop, so they leave out the rest of the journey.
a.clue: Look for the option that covers the whole journey.

b.q: Heavy rain closes a port in Queensland. A bakery in Cairns waits weeks for wheat flour that was milled elsewhere and shipped there. Which idea best explains the bakery's problem?
opts: A problem at one step in a supply chain affects later steps
Supply chains only include the steps done in one country
The bakery is the first step in the flour supply chain
Flour is made at the same place where it is sold
b.why: The port is one step in the chain, and the bakery is a later step that depends on it. A delay at the port therefore delays the flour. The bakery is the buyer at the end of the chain, not the first step.
b.clue: Think about which step the bakery depends on.

a.best: Growing, spinning, sewing, shipping and selling the shirt

b.best: A problem at one step in a supply chain affects later steps
